guide.a.listing_feeds:
When the public site is on, your listings are also published as two feeds — automatic lists that other programs can follow, so your listings show up in them without any copying:

  • Calendar feed — /feeds/listings.ics — people can add it to their calendar app (Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, and so on)
  • News feed — /feeds/listings.rss — people can follow it in a news-reading app

Both feeds include every open, running listing that is not hidden. Hidden listings are left out. The feeds update themselves as you add, change, or close listings.

guide.a.what_is_public_api:
An API is a way for a web builder's code to talk to this site directly, instead of through the pages. This one can read your listings and make bookings — the same things people do on your pages.

These answers are for your web builder. If that is not you, you can skip them.

The public endpoints below need no sign-in. There is also an admin API for managing listings, groups, and holidays — see the Admin API section below.
guide.q.get_single_listing_api: How do I read one listing?
guide.q.create_booking_api: How do I create a booking?
guide.q.api_data_exposure: What data does the API share?
guide.a.api_data_exposure: Exactly the same data as your public booking pages — nothing more. Private things like place limits, attendee counts, closing times, and webhook addresses are never included.
guide.q.where_can_i_find_the_full_api: Where can I find the full API reference?
guide.a.where_can_i_find_the_full_api: The API documentation page lists every public and admin API endpoint, with an example of what you send and what comes back for each.
guide.a.what_is_the_admin_api:
The admin API is the same as clicking around the admin pages, but done by a program. Your web builder can use it to make many changes at once, or to keep listings in step with another system.

It needs an API key — a long password made on this site — and only owners can use it.
guide.q.what_happens_to_api_keys_if_thei: What happens to API keys if their owner is deleted?
guide.a.what_happens_to_api_keys_if_thei:
Every API key belongs to the owner who made it. Delete that owner on the Users page, and their keys stop working at the same moment — any tool using one breaks straight away.

If a departing owner had keys in use, make new ones under another owner first.
guide.q.how_do_i_create_an_api_key: How do I make an API key?
guide.a.how_do_i_create_an_api_key:
Open API Keys (under Users in the navigation), give the key a name that says what it is for (for example "Zapier connection"), and click Create key.

The full key is shown only once. Copy it straight away and keep it somewhere safe — after you leave the page there is no way to see it again. Lose one, and you delete it and make a new one.
guide.q.how_do_i_authenticate: How does a program sign in?
guide.a.how_do_i_authenticate:
This one is for your web builder. The key travels in a header — an extra line of information sent with each request:

Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY

Send request bodies as JSON. A request without a working key receives 401 Invalid API key.
guide.q.what_admin_endpoints_are_availab: What can the admin API do?
guide.a.what_admin_endpoints_are_availab:
The admin API covers listings, groups, and holidays. Each can be listed, read, made, changed, and deleted:

  • GET /api/admin/listings, POST /api/admin/listings, GET /api/admin/listings/:id, PUT /api/admin/listings/:id, DELETE /api/admin/listings/:id, POST /api/admin/listings/:id/deactivate, POST /api/admin/listings/:id/reactivate, GET /api/admin/listings/:id/attendees
  • GET /api/admin/groups, POST /api/admin/groups, GET /api/admin/groups/:id, PUT /api/admin/groups/:id, DELETE /api/admin/groups/:id
  • GET /api/admin/holidays, POST /api/admin/holidays, GET /api/admin/holidays/:id, PUT /api/admin/holidays/:id, DELETE /api/admin/holidays/:id

Deletes must repeat the item's name in a confirm_identifier field — the same "type the name to confirm" rule as the pages.
guide.q.how_do_i_read_groups_and_members: How do I read groups and their members?
guide.a.how_do_i_read_groups_and_members:
Call GET /api/admin/groups. It returns every group, including hidden ones — groups with Hide from public listings list ticked. Reading a hidden group this way never makes it public.

An ordinary group's answer has no members list. Instead, every listing carries a group_ids list of its groups. To find an ordinary group's members, call GET /api/admin/listings and keep the listings whose group_ids holds that group's id. A package group adds a package_members list to its own answer, with one entry per listing in the package.

The API documentation page shows the full shape of every answer.
guide.q.how_do_i_revoke_an_api_key: How do I turn off an API key?
guide.a.how_do_i_revoke_an_api_key:
Open API Keys, find the key, and click Delete. Type the key's name to confirm.

It stops working immediately — any tool using it starts receiving 401 Invalid API key on its next try. Point tools at a new key first.

The Last used column shows when each key last worked, so you can spot dead ones before deleting.
